title: Code Girls United practice bank
about: One file for the whole bank. Question group: copy an example, change it, update answers. Code group: new question types go in practice_bank.py. Do not split into one file per category yet. Search for a category id, such as "for-range", to jump there.

categories.title: Variables
categories.blurb: A variable is a name that holds a value. print uses the name, and the output is the value.
categories.closing: Run Math when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.name: What should this variable be named, based on this code?
prompts.value: What value should we have set it to?
prompts.print_with: What should I use here if I want to print this value?
prompts.output: What is the expected output of this print?

hints.name: The variable is the name on the left of =. The value is on the right.
hints.value: Read the right side of =. Quote marks are not part of the value.
hints.print_with: Use the name. print looks up the name and shows the value. Do not put quotes around the name.
hints.output: print shows the value. It does not show the variable's name, and it does not show quote marks.

notes.name: = stores the value on the right inside the name on the left.
notes.value: That is what the variable holds after this line.
notes.print_with: Writing the value by hand skips the variable. Quotes around the name print the name itself.
notes.output: Quote marks in the code make text. They are not printed.

categories.title: Math
categories.blurb: A second line can change what the variable holds. The symbol says how.
categories.closing: Run Loops: for item in list when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.value: What is the value of the variable after the second line?
prompts.op: What does the operator in the second line do?

hints.value: Start at the first number. Apply the operator once.
hints.op: Look at the symbol between the name and the number on the second line.

notes.value: The second line stores the new number back into the same variable.
notes.op: The operator changes the current value, then the result is stored back.

categories.title: Loops: for item in list
categories.blurb: A for loop over a list runs the indented lines once per item.
categories.closing: Run the index loop when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does the indented line run?
prompts.last: What is the last line this prints?

hints.iterations: One pass per item. Count the items.
hints.last: The loop reaches the last item in the list and prints it.

notes.iterations: The header says for each item. The print is indented, so it repeats.
notes.last: Each pass holds one item. The last pass holds the last item.

meaning.prompt: What does for item in list do?
meaning.answer: One pass for each item in the list
decoys: Starts at 0 and stops before stop
Repeats while a test stays true
meaning.hint: Read the header. It names a list, not a range and not a while test.
meaning.note: The variable after for holds one item each pass, then the next item.

categories.title: Loops: index with range(len)
categories.blurb: range(len(...)) walks the indexes 0, 1, 2, and so on, so you can read list[i].
categories.closing: Run range(stop) when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does the indented line run?
prompts.last: What is the last line this prints?

hints.iterations: len(the list) is how many indexes there are. Indexes start at 0.
hints.last: The last index is one less than the length. The item at that index is last.

notes.last: The first number on the line is the index. The second is the item at that index.

meaning.hint: len gives the length. range of that length starts at 0.
meaning.note: list[i] is the item at that index. enumerate is the short form of this loop.

categories.title: Loops: range(stop)
categories.blurb: range(stop) starts at 0 and stops before stop.
categories.closing: Run range(start, stop) when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does this print?
prompts.last: What is the last number this prints?

hints.iterations: range(stop) runs stop times, starting at 0.
hints.last: It stops before stop. The last number is one less than stop.

notes.iterations: The number inside range is how many passes, because counting starts at 0.
notes.last: The last number is one less than stop. The stop number itself is not printed.

meaning.answer: 0 up to, but not including, stop
meaning.hint: One number inside range means start at 0 and stop before that number.
meaning.note: Counting starts at 0, so the last number is one less than stop.

categories.title: Loops: range(start, stop)
categories.blurb: range(start, stop) starts at start and stops before stop.
categories.closing: Run range with a step when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does this print?
prompts.first: What is the first number this prints?
prompts.last: What is the last number this prints?
prompts.includes_stop: Does this loop include the stop number?

hints.iterations: Count from start up to, but not including, stop.
hints.first: The first number inside range is the first value printed.
hints.last: The last value is one less than stop.
hints.includes_stop: The second number is the fence. The loop stops before it.

notes.iterations: Subtract start from stop. That is the number of passes.
notes.last: It prints every whole number from start until it would hit stop.
notes.includes_stop: Stop is not one of the printed numbers.

categories.title: Loops: range with a step
categories.blurb: The third number inside range is the step, including a step that counts down.
categories.closing: Run while when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does this print?
prompts.last: What is the last number this prints?
prompts.printed: What does this print, in order?

hints.iterations: Start at the first number, keep adding the step, and stop before the stop number. Count those values.
hints.last: The last value is the last one you land on before reaching stop.
hints.printed: Write each value the loop variable takes, in order.

notes.iterations: The step is the gap. A bigger step means fewer passes.
notes.last: Stop is a fence, even when the step is bigger than 1 or is negative.
notes.printed: Positive step counts up. Negative step counts down.

step_means.prompt: What does the third number inside range do?
step_means.answer: It is the step: how much to count by
decoys: It is the last number printed
It is how many times the loop runs
step_means.hint: range(start, stop, step). The third number is the gap.
step_means.note: Step 2 skips every other number. Step -1 counts down. Stop is still not printed.

categories.title: Loops: while
categories.blurb: A while loop repeats while its test is true. Something inside must change the test.
categories.closing: Run for _ in range when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does this print?
prompts.last: What is the last number this prints?
prompts.stops: When does this while loop stop?

hints.iterations: The test is checked before each pass. Count how many times it is still true.
hints.last: The last printed number is the last one that still passed the test.
hints.stops: Read the test after while. The loop stops when that test is false.

notes.iterations: Each pass prints the current number, then adds 1.
notes.last: Adding 1 moves the variable toward the end of the test.
notes.stops: The last line has to change the variable. Without it, the test would stay true.

categories.title: Loops: for _ in range
categories.blurb: _ means you want the repeats and you do not need the loop number.
categories.closing: Run the += shorthand when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does this print?

hints.iterations: The number inside range is how many passes.
hints.output: The print is indented, so each pass prints that same text.

notes.iterations: The loop variable is _, so the number itself is not used.
notes.output: Every pass prints the same text. The number of lines is the number inside range.

meaning.prompt: What does the _ in for _ in range mean?
decoys: A variable we are supposed to print
meaning.hint: _ is a name people use when they do not need the value.
meaning.note: for _ in range(4) means do the indented lines 4 times.

categories.title: Shorthand: += -= *=
categories.blurb: +=, -=, and *= are shorthand. They change the variable and store the result.
categories.closing: Run enumerate when you are ready, or run this cell again for a different example.

prompts.same_as: What is the long form of the shorthand in the loop?
prompts.value: What is the value of the variable after the loop?
prompts.iterations: How many times does the loop change the variable?

hints.same_as: += adds and stores. -= subtracts and stores. *= multiplies and stores.
hints.value: Start at the first number. Apply the change once per pass.
hints.iterations: The number inside range is how many passes.

notes.same_as: The shorthand and the long form store the same new value.
notes.value: Each pass uses the new value, not the original one.
notes.iterations: The loop variable n is not the value we are changing.

categories.title: Loops: enumerate
categories.blurb: enumerate gives you the index and the item together. Indexes still start at 0.
categories.closing: That is the path for now. Run any cell again for a different example.

prompts.iterations: How many times does the indented line run?
prompts.last: What is the last line this prints?

hints.iterations: One pass per item. Count the items.
hints.last: The first number is the index, starting at 0. The second is the item.

notes.last: The last index is one less than the length.

meaning.prompt: What does enumerate give the loop each pass?
meaning.answer: The index and the item, together
meaning.hint: Two names after for means two values each pass.
meaning.note: enumerate is the short form of for i in range(len(...)). Indexes still start at 0.
